companionBriefing: Portia only lets in people who greet her properly. Answer in Italian; mixing in English is fine while you learn.
Tap a word under her line to see what it means, or Translate sentence for the whole line. On her newest line each one uses a hint from my allowance.
The words and phrases shown beneath her lines go into your Spellbook, where you can review them later.

lines.native: Benvenuto! The mercato can wait. First, a greeting and your name. Standards, please.
lines.translation: Welcome! The market can wait. First, a greeting and your name. Standards, please.
lines.narrative: Portia’s keystone opens to reveal a visitors’ book. Her half-translated sign hangs above it, pending agreement with itself.

lines.native: Benvenuto! Greeting accepted. Now, your name, please. The book cannot file enthusiasm.
lines.translation: Welcome! Greeting accepted. Now, your name, please. The book cannot file enthusiasm.
lines.narrative: A visitors’ book slides out of Portia’s keystone. The name column remains pointedly empty.

lines.native: Piacere, Sam! Benvenuto al mercato. Your introduction is filed. Any interest in your archway’s name? Purely a manners thing.
lines.translation: Nice to meet you, Sam! Welcome to the market. Your introduction is filed. Any interest in your archway’s name? Purely a manners thing.
lines.narrative: Portia enters Sam in the visitors’ book. A second name field remains blank, with the administrative gravity of an unclaimed biscuit.

lines.native: Mi chiamo Portia. Piacere, Sam! Such manners. Benvenuto al mercato! Your paperwork is complete; mine apparently has feelings.
lines.translation: My name is Portia. Nice to meet you, Sam! Such manners. Welcome to the market! Your paperwork is complete; mine apparently has feelings.
lines.narrative: A visitors’ book slips from the keystone. Portia turns to her own entry with the flustered dignity of an official unexpectedly included in the paperwork.
